title: Tensor inheritance of the single-complex base-change condition
statement: For a cartesian square of schemes X' \xrightarrow{g'} X and S' \xrightarrow{g} S, with f:X\to S and f':X'\to S' the vertical morphisms [def-pc-base-change], let K \in D_{\mathrm{QCoh}}(\mathcal O_X) [def-pc-derived-category] and let L(g')^*K \to K' be a map in D_{\mathrm{QCoh}}(\mathcal O_{X'}). For x'\in X', put x=g'(x'), s'=f'(x') and s=f(x)=g(s'). If for every x' and i\in\mathbf Z the canonical map H^i(K_x\otimes^L_{\mathcal O_{S,s}}\mathcal O_{S',s'})\otimes_{\mathcal O_{X,x}\otimes_{\mathcal O_{S,s}}\mathcal O_{S',s'}}\mathcal O_{X',x'}\to H^i(K'_{x'}) is an isomorphism, then for every E \in D_{\mathrm{QCoh}}(\mathcal O_X), the induced map L(g')^*(E \otimes^L K) \to L(g')^*E \otimes^L K' has the same property: its corresponding canonical map at every x' and i is an isomorphism. The induced tensor map is the canonical derived-pullback tensor comparison [def-pc-derived-pullback-tensor-comparison], pinned by its K-flat representative and shared-counit equations; the assertion does not range over unrelated strong monoidal structures on the same functor.

proof.text: Obtain a canonical tensor comparison tau and its defining predicate. Realize tau by a core-monoidal model m. Function extensionality on the realization equation gives the canonical predicate for m inverse tensorator. Return m with this predicate; it fixes the morphism used in inheritance.

Fix E, coordinates d, point z and degree i. Choose coordinates c for phi using nonempty_coordinates. Apply the simultaneous ring-coordinate theorem to m inverse tensorator and its canonical predicate.

For every j, the first square and h_stalk show the original ring comparison is invertible, by cancellation of its source and target isomorphisms. Apply localizedTensorComparison_inheritance to obtain invertibility of the tensor ring comparison.
The second square makes aU.hom followed by the desired stalk comparison invertible. Cancel aU.hom to conclude IsIso for arbitrary d,z,i.

lean.statement:
theorem singleComplexInheritedTensorCondition
    [∀ Y : Scheme.{u},
      HasDerivedCategory.{w} (SheafOfModules.{u} (moduleRings Y.toRingedSpace))]
    {X X' S S' : Scheme.{u}} (f : X ⟶ S) (f' : X' ⟶ S') (g : S' ⟶ S)
    (g' : X' ⟶ X) (sq : IsPullback g' f' f g)
    (K : schemeDerivedQCohCategory X) (K' : schemeDerivedQCohCategory X')
    (φ : (derivedPullback g').obj K.obj ⟶ K'.obj)
    (h_stalk : SingleComplexBaseChange.StalkCondition f f' g g' sq K.obj K'.obj φ) :
    ∃ m : (derivedPullback g').CoreMonoidal,
      IsCanonicalPullbackTensorComparison g' (fun A B ↦ (m.μIso A B).inv) ∧
      ∀ E : schemeDerivedQCohCategory X,
        SingleComplexBaseChange.StalkCondition f f' g g' sq
          (E.obj ⊗ K.obj) (((derivedPullback g').obj E.obj) ⊗ K'.obj)
          ((m.μIso E.obj K.obj).inv ≫ ((derivedPullback g').obj E.obj ◁ φ))

statement_change.what: The previous Lean statement quantified over every monoidal structure on derived pullback. The source only states the induced canonical tensor comparison, which the existing predicate pins to the shared counit. A comparison between arbitrary tensorators does not give a square for the base-derived cohomology source. Make the canonical comparison explicit to restore the source meaning; no counterexample to the stronger all-monoidal assertion is claimed.

old_proof.text: Fix x' and write R = O_{S,s}, A = O_{X,x}, B = O_{S',s'}, and C = O_{X',x'}. The stalk of the map for E tensor^L K is obtained by first forming E_x tensor_A^L K_x, then tensoring over R with B and extending scalars to C.

source.place: Tag 0DJA, proof of part (1), local stalk computation

old_proof.text: Apply [lem-pc-derived-tensor-transitivity] with $T=A\otimes_R B$, $E=E_x$, $K=K_x$ (complexes of $A$-modules), $K'=K'_{x'}$ (a complex of $C$-modules) and $\psi:K_x\otimes_A^{L}C=(L(g')^*K)_{x'}\to K'_{x'}$ the stalk at $x'$ of the given map $L(g')^*K\to K'$ (a morphism in $D(C)$). Then $\varphi_{K_x}=\psi\circ c_{K_x}:K_x\otimes_R^{L}B\to K'_{x'}$ is the stalk map of the hypothesis, and $\beta^i_{K_x}:H^i(K_x\otimes_R^{L}B)\otimes_T C\to H^i(K'_{x'})$ is exactly the canonical map of the hypothesis, which is an isomorphism for every $i$. For $E\otimes^{L}K$, the stalk at $x'$ of $L(g')^*(E\otimes^{L}K)\to L(g')^*E\otimes^{L}K'$ is, under $(E\otimes^{L}K)_x=E_x\otimes_A^{L}K_x$, $(L(g')^*(E\otimes^L K))_{x'}=(E_x\otimes_A^{L}K_x)\otimes_A^{L}C$ and $(L(g')^*E\otimes^{L}K')_{x'}=(E_x\otimes_A^{L}C)\otimes_C^{L}K'_{x'}\cong E_x\otimes_A^{L}K'_{x'}$, the composite of the associativity isomorphism $(E_x\otimes_A^{L}K_x)\otimes_A^{L}C\cong E_x\otimes_A^{L}(K_x\otimes_A^{L}C)$ and $1_{E_x}\otimes\psi$; so its comparison map from $(E_x\otimes_A^{L}K_x)\otimes_R^{L}B$ is $\varphi_{E_x,K_x}$ of the lemma, and the canonical map of the conclusion at $(x',i)$ is $\beta^i_{E_x,K_x}:H^i((E_x\otimes_A^{L}K_x)\otimes_R^{L}B)\otimes_T C\to H^i(E_x\otimes_A^{L}K'_{x'})$. Since $C=\mathcal O_{X',x'}$ is a localization of $T$ (stalk of $X'=X\times_S S'$), it is flat over $T$ (Tag 00HT), so the flat clause of the lemma shows that $\beta^i_{E_x,K_x}$ is an isomorphism for every $i$. Since $x'$ and $i$ were arbitrary, the inherited stalkwise condition holds everywhere.
